messages:
maria_support: FYI raised by a EU customer — invoice total != dashboard total by a few cents on two invoices. Customer says the VAT breakdown lines look weird after our line-item consolidation.
raj_billing: Thanks — can you paste the invoice snippet and dashboard numbers?
maria_support: Sure, copied redacted snippet from invoice PDF: 
```
Line 1: Usage (embedding)  €0.0173  VAT 20%  €0.00346  Line total €0.02076
Line 2: Usage (generate)   €0.0052  VAT 20%  €0.00104  Line total €0.00624
Consolidated usage line (merged) shows: Subtotal €0.0225  VAT 20% €0.0045  Total €0.0270
Invoice total shows €0.0270 but dashboard (sum of raw items) = €0.02699
```
maria_support: Customer points out this scales across many small requests and they noticed a small net overcharge vs dashboard.
lucas_eng: Got it. Likely cause: we round VAT per consolidated-line after merging, while dashboard shows per-request rounded amounts then summed. Two different rounding orders -> drift.
maria_support: Is this the same as per-request rounding we saw in old tickets? This one is specific to EU VAT reallocation after line-merge.
lucas_eng: Slightly different. Repro steps I ran locally: 
1) export raw invoice lineitems for account id abc123 (billing table: invoice_line_items where invoice_id=Z)
2) simulate consolidation: group by usage_type, sum(net_amount) as raw_net, compute vat = raw_net * vat_rate, round(vat, 2) -> this is current code path
3) compare to summing per-line (round(net_i, 2); vat_i = round(net_i*vat_rate,2); sum(vat_i))
Result: consolidation vat - summed-vat = +€0.0001 to +€0.002 per invoice depending on basket composition.
lucas_eng: Example code: 
```
-- current (consolidate then round)
SELECT ROUND(SUM(net_amount), 2) AS subtotal, ROUND(ROUND(SUM(net_amount), 2) * 0.20, 2) AS vat
-- per-line (what dashboard uses)
SELECT SUM(ROUND(net_amount, 2)) AS subtotal, SUM(ROUND(ROUND(net_amount,2) * 0.20, 2)) AS vat
```
raj_billing: Hmm. That explains the sign. Dashboard shows sum of per-request rounded pieces. Invoice consolidation is doing final-round which changes distribution. Which is the correct one legally for EU VAT?
eva_finance: VAT rules vary, but many customers expect VAT per line for consumer-level receipts. For B2B it's usually okay to aggregate but we should be transparent. Need legal check.
maria_support: Customer asking for remediation: small credit or reissue? They flagged two past invoices.
lucas_eng: Proposed fix: change consolidation logic to compute vat as sum of per-line VAT (i.e., compute VAT at same granularity as dashboard), then aggregate. Implementation: when merging lineitems, carry forward the per-request VAT cents and sum them instead of re-evaluating on aggregated net. Also add a deterministic tie-breaker for rounding (bankers rounding) to avoid bias.
lucas_eng: Quick patch (billing-service) pseudo: 
```
for group in groups:
  vat_sum = sum([round(item.net * vat_rate, 2) for item in group.items])
  consolidated.net = round(sum([item.net for item in group.items]), 2)
  consolidated.vat = vat_sum
  consolidated.total = consolidated.net + consolidated.vat
```
raj_billing: That sounds reasonable. Risk: invoice PDFs will change for retro invoices if we backfill. We should avoid mass reissuance. Suggest policy: if absolute delta > €0.05, issue adjustment credit. Otherwise, note in account and include in next invoice.
eva_finance: Agreed on threshold. Also we need a customer-facing explanation template. I'll draft language: short apology, explanation that small rounding diff due to tax allocation periods and that we will credit >€0.05.
maria_support: Customer agreed to review if we share computation sample. I attached ticket #12345 (internal link: https://redwood.atlassian/billing/12345).
lucas_eng: I've created a unit test to reproduce the drift and a small branch: redwood/billing#372. Test vectors: mixed small usage lines (0.0003, 0.0017, 0.0049) across VAT 20% and 0% zones. Failing CI shows current behavior.
lucas_eng: Can @raj_billing prioritize a hotfix for next deploy window? Impact: fraction of EU invoices (~0.6% last month) with micro-deltas.
raj_billing: I'll triage. If patch + tests look good, target next release. Also prepping a short ops runbook to generate list of invoices with delta > €0.02 for manual review. Query: how to quickly get candidate invoices?
lucas_eng: Use this diagnostic SQL: 
```
WITH per_line AS (
  SELECT invoice_id, SUM(ROUND(net_amount,2) + ROUND(net_amount*vat_rate,2)) as sum_per_line
  FROM invoice_line_items
  GROUP BY invoice_id
), consolidated AS (
  SELECT invoice_id, ROUND(SUM(net_amount),2) + ROUND(ROUND(SUM(net_amount),2) * vat_rate,2) as consolidate_total
  FROM invoice_line_items
  GROUP BY invoice_id, vat_rate
)
SELECT p.invoice_id, p.sum_per_line, c.consolidate_total, p.sum_per_line - c.consolidate_total as delta
FROM per_line p JOIN consolidated c USING(invoice_id)
WHERE ABS(p.sum_per_line - c.consolidate_total) > 0.02
ORDER BY ABS(delta) DESC
```
maria_support: Perfect — I'll run that query for the affected customer and attach output.
billing-bot: Automated note: billing-test-run completed for account abc123 — 3 invoices above threshold. Link: https://billing.internal/tests/abc123-run-2026-03-17
raj_billing: Thanks. I'll coordinate finance on credits and a short message. @eva_finance please review wording.
eva_finance: Will send draft by EOD.
maria_support: Closing loop with customer for now — will update once we have fix/credits. :thumbsup:
lucas_eng: Follow-up: we should add an integration test that compares dashboard sum vs invoice PDF totals nightly for EU invoices and alert on drift > €0.05. Filed monitoring ticket.
raj_billing: Assigned to billing ops. I'll update this thread when patch ships.
maria_support: Thanks everyone.
